Residual permutation assumes exchangeable residuals after linear adjustment. Nonlinear marker-covariate relations can inflate false positives; a robust tier is internal evidence and needs independent validation.
In the patients left out of each of 200 subsamples, the whole selection procedure reached C 0.658 against 0.656 for the clinical covariates alone, a gain of +0.002 (95% CI -0.042 to 0.046). The gain is uncertain: its interval includes both no gain and a gain of 0.02 or more. Markers were selected and models refitted in each subsample; validate the locked final model independently.
More detail
WHAT TO WATCH
The selection procedure's mean subsample-to-left-out C-index gap is 0.099; the gap adjustment is a heuristic that includes training-size effects.
1,418 marker(s) were left out before testing: 1,079 near-constant (most patients at one value, as for genes expressed in few patients) and 339 constant or mostly missing.
WHAT WAS CHECKED
Family-wise p-values (Westfall-Young) from 1000 permutations, permuting each marker's residuals after regression on the clinical covariates (Smith method), approximating a conditional null.
The whole screen was repeated on 200 subsamples of 63% of the patients.
Robust: family-wise p ≤ 0.05, selected in ≥ 50% of subsamples and the same direction in ≥ 90%.
No repeated patients: no two patients have near-identical profiles over the 5,000 most variable markers.
NEXT STEPS
Validate the locked model in an independent cohort below before claiming the markers.
Report the subsample gap-adjusted C-index as a heuristic internal summary, and use locked external validation for final performance claims.
